observed_facts.statement: Both observed trials use the same commit, source SHA, immutable image ID and fingerprint, with 2 load-generator threads,64 connections,2 seconds warmup and 15 seconds measurement. The server uses CPU 0, a 1 CPU quota and 2 GiB memory/no-swap allowance.
The archived trial 2 server log is empty. The source disables access logging and sets the error-log threshold to WARN. No request trace, error message or stall timing is available from this log.

Post-stop quick_check returned ok and post count increased from 500000 to 506035 (including warmup writes). The service remained running, reported no OOM kill, and its before/after samples retain the same master/worker PIDs.

Recorded server CPU was 92.06% and RSS 99.33 MiB. The completed-response latency maximum was 27.59 ms, with p 95=7.434 ms and p 99=11.97 ms. These aggregate values do not identify the timed-out requests.
The pinned app configures one OpenResty worker and opens one SQLite handle in init_worker. SQL steps run synchronously through LuaJIT FFI, with a configured 5000 ms busy timeout.

The source allows 65000 worker connections, keepalive_timeout 75 s and 1000000 requests per keepalive connection, while this measurement uses 64 connections for 15 seconds. The saved configuration does not reveal an obvious configured limit explaining the observed counters.

A Lua routing exception is logged at ERR and mapped to HTTP 500 in the source. The observed trial has no captured HTTP errors and no captured log messages; that does not provide a trace for client-side timeouts.

inferences.confidence: possible architectural context; no causal event observed
inferences.statement: A delay in a single worker could affect multiple connections, but there is no captured evidence establishing that any shared event-loop stall occurred. The count 63, despite a 64-connection workload, does not establish that the failures were simultaneous or identify their cause.

unknowns: Which requests timed out and whether those timeout events occurred together.
Any server-side stall duration or location.
Whether SQLite I/O/checkpointing, LuaJIT/GC, CPU scheduling, networking, client timing or another factor contributed; none is established by these artifacts.
The effective wrk timeout is not explicitly configured in run.py:220-227 or stored as a value.
Per-request response/status timing for timed-out operations; access logging is disabled.
Trial 3 outcome; this diagnostic uses trials 1 and 2 only.
conclusion_for_reporting: Retain the observed trial 2 counters: 63 socket timeouts and 0 HTTP errors, with valid DB/lifecycle checks and an empty server log. No specific timeout cause is established. Keep the existing trials and let the scheduled third trial run normally.
